issues.failure_explanation: In one dimension, conformity alone imposes no neighbor-size grading. Starting with two intervals meeting at zero, repeatedly bisect only the interval immediately to the right of zero. The left interval remains unchanged, while the adjacent right interval has length 2^{-n} times its original length. All intervals remain shape regular and the mesh is conforming, but the asserted neighbor ratio and the patch generation span grow without bound.

issues.failure_explanation: The recurrences and constructed matrices use B as an approximate inverse of A. For that convention, the symmetric matrix is B^{1/2}AB^{1/2}, not B^{-1/2}AB^{-1/2}. For example, A=diag(1,t) and B=A^{-1} give right-hand condition number 1 but left-hand condition number t^2. The preceding change of variables likewise produces B^{-1}r, not the displayed Br recurrence.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the inverse-preconditioner convention consistently: replace the symmetric systems by B^{1/2}AB^{1/2}, correct the transformed variables accordingly, and retain the existing Br recurrences and bounds on BA.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted condition-number identities and the uniform bounds for the displayed inverse-scaled systems are false.
issues.title: The symmetric preconditioning formulas confuse a preconditioner with its inverse
issues.why_classification: The operational PCG guarantees have a comparable supported formulation, but the explicitly promised bounds for the inverse-scaled matrices must be replaced, not merely proved by omitted algebra.
